tagline.en: Disposable Arch, Fedora, RHEL and Ubuntu shells, on the official Toolbx images — somewhere to install a one-off tool that is not the host
tagline.pt: Shells descartáveis de Arch, Fedora, RHEL e Ubuntu, nas imagens oficiais do Toolbx — um lugar pra instalar ferramenta avulsa que não é o host

notes.en:
### Update

Each shell carries its own tag — the table above lists them. Arch is the
exception, pinned by digest because its only tag is `latest`.

### Backup

It stops the four, packs the four `/work` directories and starts them again.
There is no `.env` and no secret here to pack. A single shell can be backed up
on its own — `qh toolbx-fedora --backup --apply` — because none of them shares
a directory with the others.

### Remove

`--purge` asks for the typed name too, and deletes the `/work` of all four.
There is no tailnet node to deregister: none of these is published.
notes.pt:
### Atualizar

Cada shell tem a própria tag — a tabela acima lista todas. O Arch é a exceção,
pinado por digest porque a única tag dele é `latest`.

### Backup

Ele para as quatro, empacota os quatro `/work` e religa. Não há `.env` nem
segredo aqui para empacotar. Dá para fazer backup de um shell só — `qh
toolbx-fedora --backup --apply` — porque nenhum compartilha diretório com os
outros.
A frio de propósito: copiar banco vivo dá um arquivo que só falha na hora de
restaurar.

### Remover

O `--purge` também pede o nome digitado, e apaga o `/work` das quatro. Não há
nó de tailnet a desregistrar: nenhuma delas é publicada.

upstream.note: The official Toolbx images. None of them come from a GitHub release, so the registry's tag list is the reference. Arch has only `latest`, so it is pinned by digest and there is nothing to compare.

`registry:latest`, not `registry`: Fedora numbers its prereleases too, and publishes the stable release, the branched one and rawhide side by side — `46` is byte-identical to `rawhide` and `45` says `Prerelease` inside. The highest number is therefore always the wrong answer; asking which tag `latest` resolves to is what names the released one.
